title: PureHealth to recruit 250 Emirati graduates in UAE healthcare sector by 2028
summary: The partnership will be implemented through the National Healthcare Programme, an initiative under Nafis, the UAE’s national programme for Emiratisation.
thbAction: Pitch THB's diagnostics CRM to help labs manage doctor outreach, collection-center expansion, and B2B referral relationships while improving conversion and retention.
contentHtml:
UAE—PureHealth will recruit 250 Emirati graduates over three years from 2026 to 2028 through a partnership with the Emirati Talent Competitiveness Council, strengthening the national healthcare workforce and supporting the UAE’s Emiratisation agenda.

The partnership will be implemented through the National Healthcare Programme, an initiative under Nafis, the UAE’s national programme for Emiratisation.

It aims to connect students with healthcare employers and prepare them for professional roles through practical training, mentorship, recognised qualifications and employment opportunities during or after their studies.

The programme also provides healthcare institutions with a structured approach to developing local talent and addressing workforce requirements in specialised clinical and operational roles.

Eight healthcare specialisations targeted

Since 2026, Emirati graduates have joined PureHealth Group across eight priority disciplines: nursing, physiotherapy, pharmacy, diagnostic imaging, anaesthesia technology, medical laboratory sciences, health information management and emergency medical services.

PureHealth will deliver the initiative through its Emirati Development Center (EDC), which provides structured training, mentorship and practical experience to develop national healthcare professionals.

The platform supports career progression from entry-level positions to senior management, helping build a pipeline of skilled professionals for the country’s expanding healthcare industry.

Rashed Al Qubaisi, Group Chief Operating Officer of PureHealth, said the partnership with Nafis represents a long-term investment in the UAE’s healthcare workforce.

He noted that recruiting Emirati graduates into critical clinical and operational positions would strengthen the group’s current capabilities while developing future healthcare leaders.

Through the EDC, PureHealth aims to equip participants with the technical skills, professional experience and career development opportunities needed to take on leadership responsibilities.

Supporting private-sector Emiratisation

The partnership aligns with the UAE’s strategy to increase Emirati participation in the private sector, particularly in professions considered important to national development.

Healthcare workforce localisation also supports the country’s efforts to strengthen health system capacity, reduce reliance on external recruitment and maintain access to skilled professionals as demand for healthcare services grows.

PureHealth has already supported the career development of hundreds of Emirati professionals through the EDC.

The platform forms part of the group’s broader commitment to developing 1,000 future-ready national healthcare leaders by 2030, in line with Abu Dhabi Economic Vision 2030.

The three-year roadmap, running from 2026 to 2028, will expand opportunities for Emirati graduates across PureHealth’s healthcare operations while supporting national workforce development and private-sector employment.
